units.function: opens the paper on a quotation before any number

original_instantiations: A famous line about water everywhere and nothing fit to drink opens the page.
A famous line about water everywhere and nothing safe to drink opens the page.

units.source_excerpt: Water, water, every where, lamented the Ancient Mariner, Nor any drop to drink
units.reusable_pattern: Open on a borrowed line, then name who said it.
prohibited_generalizations: do not treat the quotation as the paper's own claim

units.function: says the danger is management, not absence

original_instantiations: What threatens the country is not an outright absence but the handling of what it has.
What threatens the country is not an outright absence but the care of what it has.

units.source_excerpt: It is not an absolute lack of water that threatens India's water security, but a challenge of managing this critical resource
units.reusable_pattern: Reject the obvious cause with it is not, then name the real one with but.
prohibited_generalizations: do not keep both causes

units.function: states the whole assignment in one sentence

original_instantiations: The job was to build a measure, project it forward, design a policy, and test that policy.
The job was to build a measure, project it forward, design a policy, and score that policy.

units.source_excerpt: Our task was to construct a mathematical model capable of measuring a country's ability to provide clean water
units.reusable_pattern: State the assignment as a chain of infinitives.
prohibited_generalizations: do not drop one of the four tasks

units.function: gives the two fits as a before and after

original_instantiations: The plain version accounted for under half; the refined one for well over two thirds.
The plain version accounted for under half; the sharpened one for well over two thirds.

units.source_excerpt: a simple two-predictor model that explained 43.7% of the variance in access to water
units.reusable_pattern: Report a refinement as the share of variance explained, before and after.
prohibited_generalizations: do not round the two percentages together

units.rhetorical_move: owns a gap and patches it
units.function: says what the model missed and how it was mended

original_instantiations: The model left warming out, so published figures were brought in to mend it.
The model left warming out, so published figures were brought in to patch it.

units.source_excerpt: Our model did not directly account for climate change, so we used published data on effects of climate change
units.reusable_pattern: Concede a gap with did not, then close it with so we used.
prohibited_generalizations: do not hide the gap

units.function: gives the result of the intervention as one percentage

original_instantiations: Running the policy forward gave a gain of a few percentage points.
Running the policy forward gave a gain of a handful of percentage points.

units.source_excerpt: resulting in a 3.78% increase in water access
units.reusable_pattern: End the summary on the single number the policy produces.
prohibited_generalizations: do not add benefits the number does not show

units.function: grounds the problem in a basic need

original_instantiations: People cannot live without safe water within reach.
People cannot get by without safe water within reach.

units.source_excerpt: Human life depends on access to clean water
units.reusable_pattern: Open the body on the dependence, in the shortest sentence available.
prohibited_generalizations: do not decorate the opening

units.function: says being near water is not the same as having safe water

original_instantiations: Sitting beside a body of water does not by itself mean the water is safe.
Sitting beside a body of water does not by itself mean the water is usable.

units.source_excerpt: presence of a freshwater body alone does not guarantee access to safe and clean water
units.reusable_pattern: Break a false equivalence with alone does not guarantee.
prohibited_generalizations: do not concede the equivalence

units.function: shows the problem crosses many fields

original_instantiations: The drivers run from the physical and the ecological across to the political and the economic.
The drivers run from the physical and the ecological across to the political and the social.

units.source_excerpt: Numerous factors, ranging from the physical and ecological to the political and socioeconomic, affect whether a country or region experiences water scarcity
units.reusable_pattern: Give the breadth of a problem with ranging from, to.
prohibited_generalizations: do not pretend the list is complete

units.function: says earlier efforts helped some and failed others

original_instantiations: Earlier efforts have helped in places and still left many behind.
Earlier efforts have helped in places and still left many unserved.

units.source_excerpt: attempts by the government and other organizations have had some success, but have failed to solve the problem for many
units.reusable_pattern: Credit earlier work and cap it with but have failed.
prohibited_generalizations: do not dismiss the earlier work entirely

units.function: says the models grow more complex in a series

original_instantiations: We meet the problem with a run of regressions, each one heavier than the last.
We meet the problem with a run of regressions, each one fuller than the last.

units.source_excerpt: we address the challenge by developing a series of regression models of increasing complexity
units.reusable_pattern: Preview the method as a series that grows more complex.
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim the last model is complete

units.function: justifies simplifying before listing the assumptions

original_instantiations: No model can hold every relevant factor, so we cut and simplified.
No model can hold every relevant factor, so we trimmed and simplified.

units.source_excerpt: It is impossible to fully model every possible relevant factor. As such, we made several assumptions and simplifications
units.reusable_pattern: Justify the assumptions by declaring full coverage impossible.
prohibited_generalizations: do not pretend the simplification is free

units.function: states the four things a linear fit demands

original_instantiations: A straight-line fit demands linearity, no correlation among predictors, normal data and normal errors.
A straight-line fit demands linearity, no correlation among predictors, normal data and normal residuals.

units.source_excerpt: we must assume that all variables included are linearly related, that none of our predictor variables are correlated, the data are normally distributed, and the errors are normally distributed
units.reusable_pattern: List the conditions a method smuggles in, with we must assume.
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim the conditions were tested

units.function: says access stands in for scarcity, reversed

original_instantiations: We let the share with safe water stand for scarcity, flipped.
We let the share with safe water stand for scarcity, reversed.

units.source_excerpt: we assume that percent of population with access to clean water is a direct (inverse) proxy for water scarcity
units.reusable_pattern: Name a proxy and mark its direction in parentheses.
prohibited_generalizations: do not leave the direction unmarked

units.function: says the fitted links hold for the forecast window

original_instantiations: We take the fitted links to hold for at least the next fifteen years.
We take the fitted links to hold for at least the coming fifteen years.

units.source_excerpt: we assume that the relationships between variables will remain consistent for at least the next fifteen years
units.reusable_pattern: Bound a forecast assumption with for at least.
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim the links hold forever

units.function: says what each predictor stands for

original_instantiations: Growth stands in for rising demand, and income per person for the means to meet it.
Growth stands in for rising demand, and income per person for the capacity to meet it.

units.source_excerpt: we assume that population growth is a direct proxy for clean water demand and that GDP per capita is a direct proxy for a country's ability to meet that demand
units.reusable_pattern: Pair each predictor with the thing it stands for.
prohibited_generalizations: do not add proxies the model does not use

units.function: says an interdisciplinary problem needs careful definitions

original_instantiations: Because the problem crosses fields, the terms have to be pinned down with care.
Because the problem crosses fields, the terms have to be fixed with care.

units.source_excerpt: Because water scarcity is a complicated interdisciplinary problem, it is important to exercise care in operationally defining one's terms
units.reusable_pattern: Precede a definition list with the reason care is needed.
prohibited_generalizations: do not define terms without saying why

units.function: fixes what access means in this paper

original_instantiations: In this paper, having water means actively using an improved source.
In this paper, having water means actively drawing on an improved source.

units.source_excerpt: Access to water is the percentage of a country's population actively using an improved water source
units.reusable_pattern: Define the target quantity in one sentence with a citation behind it.
prohibited_generalizations: do not leave the target undefined

units.function: says each model is the base for the next

original_instantiations: The plain version gave a crude view, and we built the fuller one on top of it.
The plain version gave a crude view, and we built the richer one on top of it.

units.source_excerpt: The Basic Model provides an extremely simplified view, but served as the basis on which we built the Refined Model
units.reusable_pattern: Describe a simple model as the base the next one stands on.
reusable_elements: served as the basis on which we built
prohibited_generalizations: do not discard the simple model

units.function: says the first model exists to be beaten

original_instantiations: The first model was only there to be beaten and to show where the method breaks.
The first model was only there to be surpassed and to show where the method breaks.

units.source_excerpt: our goal was simply to establish a baseline against which to measure the improvements of our Refined Model and to quickly locate the limitations of our technique
units.reusable_pattern: Give a baseline two jobs: to be beaten, and to expose the method.
prohibited_generalizations: do not present the baseline as the answer

units.function: turns a coefficient into a one-unit effect

original_instantiations: One extra percentage point of growth goes with a drop of several points in access, everything else held fixed.
One extra percentage point of growth goes with a fall of several points in access, everything else held fixed.

units.source_excerpt: an increase in the rate of a country's population growth by one percentage point is, on average, associated with a 5.35% decrease in access to water, holding all other variables constant
units.reusable_pattern: Translate a slope as a one-unit change associated with an effect, everything else held constant.
prohibited_generalizations: do not read the slope as a cause

units.function: says the signs match common sense

original_instantiations: The signs agree with common sense once each predictor is read as its proxy.
The signs agree with ordinary sense once each predictor is read as its proxy.

units.source_excerpt: These results make intuitive sense if one considers GDP per capita a proxy for a country's economic ability
units.reusable_pattern: Confirm a result by saying it makes intuitive sense, and give the reading that makes it so.
prohibited_generalizations: do not treat intuition as proof

units.function: says twenty candidates were cut to the best subset

original_instantiations: We started with twenty candidates and kept the subset with the best adjusted fit.
We started with twenty candidates and held the subset with the best adjusted fit.

units.source_excerpt: we chose a set of twenty variables to consider as possible predictors. We then chose the subset of these variables resulting in the highest adjusted R2 value
units.reusable_pattern: Describe variable selection as a pool, then a criterion.
reusable_elements: the subset resulting in the highest
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim every candidate was informative

units.function: says which function did the cutting

original_instantiations: The cutting was done by a subset search in the software we used.
The trimming was done by a subset search in the software we used.

units.source_excerpt: we culled the subset with the highest adjusted R2 value using the regsubsets function in R
units.reusable_pattern: Name the function and the software when a step is automated.
prohibited_generalizations: do not hide the tool

units.function: explains how one gap was filled

original_instantiations: One variable had no value for the year, so we averaged the year before and the year after.
One variable had no value for the year, so we averaged the year prior and the year after.

units.source_excerpt: In order to repair this deficiency, we took the arithmetic mean of 2011 and 2013 values for each country
units.reusable_pattern: Describe a data repair as the deficiency and then the arithmetic.
prohibited_generalizations: do not present the fill as observed data

units.function: argues the fill adds less error than the alternative

original_instantiations: A gap of a single year adds less error than mixing years would.
A gap of a single year adds less error than blending years would.

units.source_excerpt: we are confident that this estimation introduces a smaller error into our model than would using data from different years
units.reusable_pattern: Defend a repair by comparing its error with the alternative.
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim the fill is exact

units.function: says a positive slope was expected to be negative

original_instantiations: One slope came out positive where sense says negative, and we take that as a side effect of the fit.
One slope came out positive where sense says negative, and we read that as a side effect of the fit.

units.source_excerpt: the coefficient for air pollution is a positive number, where one would intuitively expect a negative number, but we consider this a byproduct of the multiple regression
units.reusable_pattern: Flag a wrong-way sign and attribute it instead of hiding it.
prohibited_generalizations: do not silently drop the odd sign

units.function: shifts the blame from nature to institutions

original_instantiations: The coming crisis is, in the main, of people's own making.
The coming crisis is, in the main, of human making.

units.source_excerpt: the impending water crisis in India is predominantly a manmade problem
units.reusable_pattern: Attribute a crisis with predominantly, so the claim stays short of total.
prohibited_generalizations: do not say entirely manmade

units.function: ranks one driver above the rest

original_instantiations: Population growth is by a wide margin the gravest threat.
Population growth is by a wide margin the largest threat.

units.source_excerpt: India's population growth is easily the leading threat to water security
units.reusable_pattern: Rank a driver with easily the leading.
prohibited_generalizations: do not rank without a reason nearby

units.rhetorical_move: sets a number against a threshold
units.function: shows the supply already sits below a known line

original_instantiations: The supply already sits under the line that marks a country as stressed.
The supply already sits beneath the line that marks a country as stressed.

units.source_excerpt: the current water supply in India is less than 1,000 cubic meters per person, already less than the 1,700 cubic meter per person threshold
units.reusable_pattern: Compare a value with a named threshold and stress the already.
prohibited_generalizations: do not invent the threshold

units.rhetorical_move: removes the case to test it
units.function: explains the out-of-sample check

original_instantiations: Because the country sat inside the sample, we refit without it to test the projection.
Because the country sat inside the sample, we refit without it to check the projection.

units.source_excerpt: Because India was included in the 147 countries in our model, we re-ran the regression with India's values removed
units.reusable_pattern: Justify a refit by the contamination it removes.
prohibited_generalizations: do not call it out-of-sample without the removal

units.function: argues a mismatch still backs the model

original_instantiations: The figures miss the published one, yet they sit close enough to each other to trust.
The figures miss the published one, yet they land close enough to each other to trust.

units.source_excerpt: Though our model's values for 2012 do not match the actual values, they are close enough to each other that we don't feel the model is significantly influenced
units.reusable_pattern: Concede a mismatch with though, then limit the damage.
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim an exact match

units.function: says each predictor is projected on its own past

original_instantiations: Each predictor was projected from its own past, the latest year on the ten before it.
Each predictor was projected from its own history, the latest year on the ten before it.

units.source_excerpt: we ran a regression for each predictor using its most recent value as the dependent variable and the previous 10 years of values as independent variables
units.reusable_pattern: Describe an autoregression by naming the dependent year and the window.
prohibited_generalizations: do not call it a forecast without the window

units.function: justifies freezing one predictor

original_instantiations: With little data, we took the supply as steady and held the recent average fixed.
With little data, we took the supply as steady and held the recent mean fixed.

units.source_excerpt: we assumed that the total water supply of a country should remain relatively constant. As such, we averaged the 2012 and 2013 values and held that value constant
units.reusable_pattern: Freeze a predictor only after saying why it should not move.
prohibited_generalizations: do not freeze a variable silently

units.rhetorical_move: fills a short series with a rate
units.function: says a constant rate stands in for a missing regression

original_instantiations: Too few years for a fit, so we carried the past rate forward.
Too few years for a fit, so we ran the past rate forward.

units.source_excerpt: we lacked sufficient data for an autoregression, so we assumed the percentage of people without access to electricity would decrease at the same rate
units.reusable_pattern: Replace a missing fit with a constant rate, and say the data were lacking.
prohibited_generalizations: do not present the rate as fitted

units.function: says the forecast rises where others warn of crisis

original_instantiations: Our projection rises, which clashes with warnings of a coming crisis.
Our projection rises, which conflicts with warnings of a coming crisis.

units.source_excerpt: the positive trend in our forecast is at odds with other forecasts of an impending water crisis
units.reusable_pattern: Set the paper's own result against the consensus with at odds with.
prohibited_generalizations: do not bury the disagreement

units.function: blames the gap on what is being measured

original_instantiations: We read the gap as a difference in what is being counted, not in the arithmetic.
We read the gap as a difference in what is being measured, not in the arithmetic.

units.source_excerpt: we interpret this difference in projections as a result of differing metrics of water scarcity
units.reusable_pattern: Resolve a clash by pointing at the metric, not the number.
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim the other forecasts are wrong

units.function: says water scarcity reaches past drinking

original_instantiations: Most of the freshwater goes to farming, so the shortage reaches the food supply too.
Most of the freshwater goes to farming, so the shortage reaches the harvest too.

units.source_excerpt: About 70% of the world's freshwater supply is used in agriculture. Water scarcity, then, plays a significant role in feeding the world's population
units.reusable_pattern: Move from a share to its consequence with then.
prohibited_generalizations: do not stop at the drinking-water frame

units.function: drops the idea of adding water

original_instantiations: Moving water long distances wastes it, and the region is not dry, so we chase no extra water.
Moving water long distances wastes it, and the region is not arid, so we chase no extra water.

units.source_excerpt: it is generally inefficient to transport large quantities of water long distances. Therefore, we do not consider any methods for increasing the absolute quantity of water
units.reusable_pattern: Decline an option with therefore we do not consider, after the reason.
prohibited_generalizations: do not dismiss the option without the reason

units.function: says only two of the proposals were tested

original_instantiations: Short on time and facing a wide plan, we tested only two of the proposals.
Short on time and facing a broad plan, we tested only two of the proposals.

units.source_excerpt: Because of time constraints and due to the large scope of our intervention plan, we chose to use our model to test two of the interventions
units.reusable_pattern: Limit the tested set and give both reasons.
prohibited_generalizations: do not imply the untested proposals failed

units.function: trusts the ranking but not the exact level

original_instantiations: We trust the ranking of the effects and not the exact level.
We trust the ordering of the effects and not the exact level.

units.source_excerpt: Though we are not convinced that our model accurately measures the precise amount, we are convinced that it accurately demonstrates the relative impacts
units.reusable_pattern: Split convinced from not convinced in one sentence.
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim both at once

units.function: says the two policies together beat either one

original_instantiations: Each policy helped on its own, and the two together helped more than either.
Each policy helped on its own, and the pair together helped more than either.

units.source_excerpt: both of the interventions we modeled each improved access to water, and the conjunction of both interventions resulted in a greater improvement than either did alone
units.reusable_pattern: Compare a combination against its parts with greater than either alone.
prohibited_generalizations: do not report only the combined figure

units.rhetorical_move: says the policy cancels the damage
units.function: reports the interventions offset the climate loss

original_instantiations: The two policies together wiped out the projected loss from warming.
The two policies together cancelled the projected loss from warming.

units.source_excerpt: the introduction of both interventions completely mitigated the predicted effects of climate change
units.reusable_pattern: Report a full offset with completely mitigated.
prohibited_generalizations: do not say the damage was reversed past the baseline unless shown

units.function: warns that a partial policy could backfire

original_instantiations: Pursue only some of the policies and the richer economy could worsen the warming.
Pursue only part of the policies and the richer economy could worsen the warming.

units.source_excerpt: if only some of the interventions are pursued, or if they are pursued incompletely, an increase in economic productivity could increase carbon dioxide emissions
units.reusable_pattern: Attach a warning to the partial case with if only.
prohibited_generalizations: do not let the warning swallow the result

units.function: gives the with-country and without-country figures side by side

original_instantiations: Left out, the country scores a little lower than when it is kept in, and the two sit close.
Left out, the country scores a little under the figure from when it is kept in, and the two sit close.

units.source_excerpt: With India's values removed, our model suggests that 83.2% of India's population should have had access to water, while the version with India's values included suggests 84.2%
units.reusable_pattern: Report a sensitivity check as the two numbers and the gap between them.
prohibited_generalizations: do not report only one of the two runs

units.function: turns one published projection into a yearly rate

original_instantiations: We spread the published projection evenly and got a small loss each year.
We spread the published projection evenly and got a slight loss each year.

units.source_excerpt: Assuming that both increase in temperature and decrease in availability of water follow a linear trend, we determined a 0.149% decrease in access to water per year
units.reusable_pattern: Show a yearly rate as the even spread of a published total.
prohibited_generalizations: do not hide the linearity assumption

units.function: says warming hurts and the policies more than undo it

original_instantiations: Adding warming made things worse, and the policies more than undid that.
Adding warming made things worse, and the policies more than repaired that.

units.source_excerpt: When we introduced climate change into the model, the prospects of access to water worsened. However, the introduction of both interventions completely mitigated the predicted effects
units.reusable_pattern: Set the damage and the remedy in consecutive sentences.
prohibited_generalizations: do not merge the two effects into one number

units.function: refuses a single cause

original_instantiations: No one cause is to blame; the crisis is a pile-up of things otherwise unrelated.
No one cause is to blame; the crisis is a heap of things otherwise unrelated.

units.source_excerpt: India's water crisis is not caused by any single factor. Instead, it is an interdisciplinary problem resulting from a perfect storm of otherwise unrelated variables
units.reusable_pattern: Refuse a single cause, then rename the problem.
reusable_elements: not caused by any single factor
prohibited_generalizations: do not then name a single cause

units.function: says the numbers are rough but the trends are clear

original_instantiations: The levels are rough, but the direction of the trends is plain.
The levels are rough, but the direction of the trends is clear.

units.source_excerpt: it used a representative cross-section of the available data to show inexact values, but clearly-defined trends
units.reusable_pattern: Separate what is inexact from what is clear in one sentence.
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim precision for the levels

units.function: says some needed figures were absent

original_instantiations: Some of the figures the model needed were simply not in the public sources.
Some of the figures the model needed were simply absent from the public sources.

units.source_excerpt: some of the necessary data in our model was missing from our publicly-available sources
units.reusable_pattern: Locate a data gap in the source, not in the effort.
prohibited_generalizations: do not blame the gap on the model

units.function: says stand-ins should be replaced by direct measures

original_instantiations: The stand-in variables ought to be swapped for direct measures next time.
The stand-in variables ought to be replaced by direct measures next time.

units.source_excerpt: some of our variables were used as proxy variables. In the next model, these proxy variables should be replaced with more direct measures
units.reusable_pattern: Mark a proxy as temporary and name its replacement.
prohibited_generalizations: do not treat a proxy as the real quantity

units.function: says no model will capture the whole problem

original_instantiations: No one model is ever likely to capture the whole of the problem.
No one model is ever likely to hold the whole of the problem.

units.source_excerpt: No single model will likely ever be able to fully account for the complexity of water scarcity
units.reusable_pattern: Cap the work with a limit on what any model can do.
prohibited_generalizations: do not promise completeness later

units.function: says the decisive factors are socioeconomic

original_instantiations: The model says improvement is possible, and the factors that matter most are socioeconomic.
The model says improvement is possible, and the factors that count most are socioeconomic.

units.source_excerpt: Our model shows that it is possible to improve India's water situation and that the most important factors in need of intervention are socioeconomic
units.reusable_pattern: Close on what is possible and on which factors matter most.
prohibited_generalizations: do not name a factor the model never used

units.function: puts culture and infrastructure above the climate

original_instantiations: Warming will make it worse, yet the harder job is the attitudes and the infrastructure.
Warming will make it worse, yet the larger job is the attitudes and the infrastructure.

units.source_excerpt: Even though climate change will worsen the problem, the greatest challenge is to develop the cultural attitudes and to build the critical infrastructure
units.reusable_pattern: Concede the climate, then rank the human task above it with the greatest challenge.
prohibited_generalizations: do not dismiss the climate effect

units.function: states the point of ever-finer models

original_instantiations: Finer models exist so that, eventually, nobody need fear for safe water.
Finer models exist so that, eventually, nobody need worry over safe water.

units.source_excerpt: through efforts to develop increasingly accurate and refined models, no human being should ever have to worry about access to clean water
units.reusable_pattern: End by tying the technical work to the human outcome.
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim the outcome is already reached

units.function: closes the paper with the works cited

original_instantiations: The works drawn on are set out one by one.
The works drawn on are set down one by one.

units.source_excerpt: References
units.reusable_pattern: Close with a numbered list of the works used.
prohibited_generalizations: do not treat the list as an argument
